narrative:
The model estimates a 66% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that, in combination, signal a higher risk of departure compared to colleagues who are expected to stay.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while at your current employer. This stands out because most employees predicted to stay (77%) report receiving no such offers, suggesting external options make it easier to consider leaving. Next, your 11+ years of total professional experience also pushes the prediction toward leaving. While this is valuable, only 15% of employees expected to stay have this much experience, indicating the model sees longer-tenured professionals as more likely to explore new horizons. Finally, working in the "other" sector contributes to the prediction of leaving. This sector represents just 22% of those predicted to stay, compared to higher concentrations in medical and education fields that appear more stable.

Taken together, these elements outweigh positive signals such as your sense of having received deserved promotions, useful training, and high environmental satisfaction. The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as exploring internal growth paths that match external offers. You may wish to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your long-term goals given the opportunities available to you. (248 words)
